controls.reason: Identifying every affected asset, artifact, device and relying party requires a complete, current cryptographic dependency and deployment inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The structured impact record can list all registered objects while an offline device or undocumented relying party still trusts the compromised key, so the record passes while impact coverage is incomplete.

controls.reason: The rule leaves both the meaning of regularly and the success oracle for emergency rotation and recovery tests unspecified.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A team can record an annual exercise that invokes both loss scenarios but never restores an offline consumer; the generic test record passes although cadence and recovery effectiveness may be unacceptable.

controls.reason: Preventing every old backup restore from reintroducing five classes of revoked or vulnerable state requires exhaustive backup and restore-path coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Tests for all registered backup jobs can pass while an untracked operator snapshot restores an old trust anchor or vulnerable binary into production.

controls.reason: A root-cause review requires causal judgment, and updating seven artifacts correctly requires deciding which changes the incident evidence actually warrants.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All seven documents can receive timestamp-only edits and the review can name the immediate fault while missing the systemic cause; presence checks would pass a substantively broken response.

controls.reason: The release decision depends on contextual materiality and on proving complete discovery and ownership of cryptographic uses, keys, data and dependencies.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every recorded material item can have an owner while an undocumented signing key is incorrectly deemed immaterial; the gate passes although a material cryptographic dependency remains uninventoried.

controls.reason: Absence of embedded keys across source, artifacts, clients, logs, tickets, documents and storage is an open-world negative claim over incomplete repositories.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Configured secret scanners can report clean results while an encoded key remains in an archived ticket attachment or compiled client asset outside their recognized formats.

controls.reason: Whether the six cryptographic failures are known or reasonably suspected requires specialist interpretation of incomplete evidence and adversarial behavior.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All tracked findings can be closed and bounded tests can pass while repeated ciphertext patterns reasonably indicate nonce reuse that the configured oracle does not recognize.

controls.reason: Verification of recovery, consumer adoption, dependent artifacts and rollback implications requires complete inventories plus substantive operational impact judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered consumers can acknowledge the new key and a recovery drill can pass while an offline verifier and archived signed artifact are omitted, making rotation irreversible for them.
